Growth is an increase in body size, from an increase in cell number and cell size. It is measured by weight, length or height, and head circumference.
From birth to 28 days of life.
In infancy (the first year of life). There is a second peak at the pubertal growth spurt.
What is the normal height velocity in mid-childhood?
5–7 cm per year. A velocity below 4 cm per year before puberty is abnormal.
What is the most important postnatal factor that affects growth?
Nutrition: protein–energy malnutrition and poor complementary feeding.
Which hormone mainly drives fetal growth?
Insulin, together with the insulin-like growth factors (IGFs). Growth hormone has little effect before birth.
Which hormone fuses the epiphyses and stops growth?
Oestrogen, in both boys and girls.
Up to what age is length measured lying down?
Under 2 years of age, supine on a length board.
For how long is the growth chart corrected for prematurity?
Until 2 years of age; the measurements are plotted at the corrected age.
What is the average birth weight of a term baby?
3–3.5 kg. Low birth weight is a birth weight below 2.5 kg.
How much weight does a newborn lose after birth, and when is it regained?
Up to 10% of the birth weight in the first 3–4 days (physiological weight loss). The birth weight is regained by 10–14 days.
When does the birth weight double, triple and quadruple?
It doubles at 4–5 months, triples at 1 year and quadruples at 2 years.
What is the monthly weight gain in the first 4 months?
About ¾ kg per month (25–30 g per day).

What is the length at birth and at 1 year?
50 cm at birth and 75 cm at 1 year: an increase of 25 cm in the first year.

How is the mid-parental height of a boy calculated?
(Father's height + mother's height) ÷ 2 + 6.5 cm. The expected range is ± 10 cm.
What is the upper-to-lower segment ratio at birth, and when does it reach 1?
It is 1.7 at birth and reaches 1.0 at 7–10 years.

What is the head circumference at birth and at 1 year?
35 cm at birth and 47 cm at 1 year: an increase of 12 cm in the first year.
How fast does the head circumference grow in the first year?
2 cm per month from 0 to 3 months, 1 cm per month from 3 to 6 months and 0.5 cm per month from 6 to 12 months.
When are the head and chest circumferences equal?
At about 1 year. After that, the chest circumference is larger.

What are the perinatal and postnatal causes of microcephaly?
Perinatal: birth asphyxia (hypoxic–ischaemic encephalopathy). Postnatal: meningitis and encephalitis.
Name three bony (skull) causes of macrocephaly.
Rickets, chronic haemolytic anaemia (thalassaemia) and achondroplasia.

Which X-ray is used to assess bone age after 1 year of age?
An X-ray of the left hand and wrist, read with the Greulich–Pyle atlas.

What are the causes of an advanced bone age?
Precocious puberty, congenital adrenal hyperplasia, hyperthyroidism and obesity.
What is the mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) cut-off for severe acute malnutrition in children aged 6–59 months?
A MUAC below 11.5 cm (the red zone).
What is the normal range on a WHO growth chart?
Between −2 and +2 standard deviations (about the 3rd to 97th centile), with the child following his or her own channel.
Which growth indicator shows chronic malnutrition?
Length- or height-for-age: a low value is stunting.
Which growth indicator shows acute malnutrition?
Weight-for-length or weight-for-height: a low value is wasting.
How is growth faltering recognised on a growth chart?
The weight crosses two major centile lines downwards, or the weight curve becomes flat.
A child is short but overweight for his height. Which group of causes should be considered?
An endocrine cause: hypothyroidism, growth hormone deficiency or Cushing syndrome.
